titulo: The map of the cases: Dative and instrumental: the essentials

aula.objetivo: Understand what cases are, see the map of the six cases, and recognise which case appears, and why, in sentences you already know.

blocos.titulo: Special cases (мать, дочь) and support tables for the accusative
blocos.explicacao: Special cases. МАТЬ and ДОЧЬ. Two feminine words in -ь. In the singular they behave like any other feminine in -ь: they do not change. Мать is мать, дочь is дочь. In the plural they are irregular: the accusative plural is матере́й and дочере́й (the same as the genitive plural). You only need to remember this when you reach the plural. ДИТЯ. Дитя́ (child) is the only neuter word that names a person. In the accusative singular it stays дитя́ (the same as the nominative). In the plural it is дете́й (the same as the genitive plural). It is an exception, but you already know that дитя is special. СУДЬЯ. Судья́ (judge) is masculine in meaning but feminine in form (it ends in -я). In the accusative it changes like a feminine noun: судью́. Support tables: personal pronouns, adjectives and possessives in the accusative. English comparison: this is the part English still has. Just as "he" becomes "him" and "she" becomes "her", Russian я becomes меня́ and она́ becomes её.

blocos.titulo: Common accusative mistakes, sentences and summary chart
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: The mistakes English speakers WILL make in the accusative. Mistake 1: using the nominative instead of the accusative for a feminine noun. ❌ Wrong: Я ви́жу кни́га. ✅ Right: Я ви́жу кни́гу. English nouns never change after the verb, so you think "book is book". But a feminine noun always changes in Russian. Always. Mistake 2: not changing an animate masculine. ❌ Wrong: Я ви́жу друг. ✅ Right: Я ви́жу дру́га. A "friend" has a soul. It changes. Always. Mistake 3: changing an inanimate masculine. ❌ Wrong: Я ви́жу до́ма. ✅ Right: Я ви́жу дом. A "house" has no soul. It does not change. Never. Mistake 4: forgetting that the neuter never changes. ❌ Wrong: Я ви́жу окна́. ✅ Right: Я ви́жу окно́. The neuter never changes. Never. Mistake 5: thinking that the feminine in -ь changes. ❌ Wrong: Я ви́жу дверю́. ✅ Right: Я ви́жу дверь. The feminine in -ь stays the same as the nominative. Mistake 6: applying the animate-masculine rule to a feminine word that names an animal. ❌ Wrong: Я ви́жу соба́к. The dog has a soul, so you might want to add a letter like for a masculine. But соба́ка is feminine, and a feminine always follows the feminine rule: а → у. ✅ Right: Я ви́жу соба́ку. The soul only matters for masculine nouns. Mistake 7: not telling an animate masculine from an inanimate one. This is the most serious error. Both стол and друг end in a consonant, and you cannot see the difference by looking. The magic question solves it: does стол have a soul? No. Does друг have a soul? Yes. STEP 2: Full sentences with the accusative. Now real sentences, to see the accusative at work. STEP 3: Summary chart: the accusative case.

blocos.titulo: Dative and instrumental: just the essentials
blocos.explicacao: The dative answers «кому?» (to whom, for whom): masculine -у or -ю (брат → брату), feminine -е (мама → маме). The pronouns change a lot: я → мне, ты → тебе, он → ему, она → ей, мы → нам, вы → вам, они → им. One important sentence: «Мне нравится музыка» (literally «to me is pleasing the music» = I like music). The instrumental answers «кем?» and is the form for «with someone» (with = «с»): masculine -ом or -ем (брат → с братом), feminine -ой or -ей (мама → с мамой). This is only a first contact: each case will get its own lessons.

exemplos.pt: I give the book to my brother.

blocos.ru: У меня есть друг. Его зовут Иван. Я часто звоню ему. Мы любим гулять вместе. Иван работает с братом. Мне нравится Иван.
blocos.pt: I have a friend. His name is Ivan. I often call him. We like to walk together. Ivan works with his brother. I like Ivan.

blocos.enunciado: Say: «Я звоню маме. Я работаю с другом. Мне нравится музыка.»
Write 4 sentences with the genitive (нет, без, для, около).
